calls.body: The Ducks are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at keeping shots away. Our lean: the Ducks’ shot volume wins out.

calls.head: Sheltered vs. Exposed
calls.body: The Golden Knights keep dangerous shots away, but the Ducks give up a lot of them. Vegas is the league’s best for preventing dangerous shots, and Anaheim is near the bottom. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should come at the Ducks’ net.
calls.call: The Golden Knights prevent dangerous shots better than the Ducks do.

surprises.head: Anaheim found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Vegas is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: Anaheim’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (about 5.8% against Vegas) and a league average of 6.2%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: The Ducks survive a Golden Knights rally
paras: This one got way too interesting for the Ducks. Jeff Malott made his Ducks debut, after two seasons with the Kings. Beckett Sennecke struck first for the Ducks with just eight seconds left in the first. Alex Killorn, Malott and Leo Carlsson scored three goals in less than six minutes early in the second to make it 4-0. Shea Theodore got the Golden Knights on the board early in the third, and the goal stood after the Ducks challenged for offside. Tomáš Hertl cut Anaheim’s lead to 4-2 on the power play a minute and a half later. Braeden Bowman pulled the Knights within one with just under three minutes left, but the Ducks held on. Noah Warren played his first NHL game and picked up a point. A.J. Greer made his Ducks debut, after two seasons with the Panthers, and picked up an assist.

The Golden Knights outshot the Ducks 30-20, but the Ducks’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Lukáš Dostál made 27 saves for the Ducks, and Carter Hart stopped 16 of 20. By our Swing measure, Tristan Luneau had the best night of anyone. The Ducks improved to 1-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage. The Golden Knights fell to 1-1-0, giving up the best points percentage in the NHL to the Ducks.

items.text: It was the Ducks’ first game of the season.
Jack Eichel extended his point streak against Anaheim to nine games.
The Ducks have beaten the Golden Knights four straight times, going back to last season.
The Ducks’ Judd Caulfield played his first NHL game.
